content_units: Best Laptop Pick for a CS Student

For your priorities—  under $1,200  ,   16GB RAM minimum  ,   good battery life  , and enough performance for   programming, light Docker, and occasional photo editing  —the   MacBook Air M2   is the best overall fit if you’re comfortable with macOS.
If you want the best   Windows value  , the   Acer Swift Go 14   is the strongest balance.
Ranked Laptop Comparison
Rank   Laptop   Price   Weight   Battery   Best For   Main Trade-off
1   MacBook Air M2   USD 1,199   1.24kg   15-hour claimed   Best all-around mix of battery, portability, and smooth everyday dev work   Near your budget cap; macOS may not suit every workflow
2   Acer Swift Go 14   USD 899   1.3kg   11-hour claimed   Best Windows balance for student use, portability, and battery   Less raw performance than the ASUS for heavier sustained workloads
3   ASUS Vivobook Pro 15   USD 1,099   1.8kg   7-hour battery   Best for stronger performance and photo-editing headroom   Heavier and noticeably worse battery life
4   Lenovo ThinkBook 14 Gen 6   USD 849   1.4kg   9-hour battery   Best budget-friendly practical choice   Good overall, but not class-leading in battery or performance versus the others
Why This Ranking Fits Your Use Case
1) MacBook Air M2
-   Why it ranks first:   It gives you the best combination of   battery life  ,   portability  , and   real-world responsiveness   for coding, many CS student workflows, and light creative work.
-   Programming:   Excellent for editors, IDEs, web dev, Python, and general coursework.
-   Light Docker:   Fine for light container use, though compatibility can occasionally be less straightforward than on native x86 Windows/Linux setups.
-   Photo editing:   Very good for occasional editing thanks to strong efficiency and display quality typically associated with this class.
-   Main trade-off:   You’re paying almost the full budget, and   macOS   may be a downside if you need Windows-only tools or prefer easier x86 virtualization behavior.
2) Acer Swift Go 14
-   Why it ranks second:   Best   Windows all-rounder   here for a CS student.
-   Programming:   More than enough for coding, browser-heavy workflows, office use, and school projects.
-   Light Docker:   Suitable for light containers and local dev environments with 16GB RAM.
-   Photo editing:   Good for occasional editing, though not as performance-oriented as the ASUS.
-   Main trade-off:   It’s balanced rather than specialized; if you start doing heavier editing or more sustained container workloads, it has less headroom than the Vivobook Pro 15.
-   Best value pick   overall.
3) ASUS Vivobook Pro 15
-   Why it ranks third:   Strongest raw performance of the Windows options listed, and   1TB SSD   is a real advantage for projects, Docker images, and photo files.
-   Programming:   Excellent for heavier local workloads.
-   Light Docker:   Best suited of the Windows group if your Docker usage grows beyond “light.”
-   Photo editing:   Best option here for that task among the Windows models.
-   Main trade-off:     Weight and battery  . At 1.8kg and 7 hours claimed, it’s much less convenient for long campus days.
4) Lenovo ThinkBook 14 Gen 6
-   Why it ranks fourth:   It’s still a solid option and meets your baseline requirements well.
-   Programming:   Easily capable for general CS coursework.
-   Light Docker:   Adequate, though less compelling than the ASUS for heavier multitasking.
-   Photo editing:   Fine for light use.
-   Main trade-off:   It doesn’t clearly win in any major category: battery is decent but not best, portability is fine but not best, and performance is good but not standout versus the field.
Final Recommendation by Priority
Best overall: MacBook Air M2
Choose this if:
- You want the   best battery life
- You value   light weight
- You’re okay with   macOS
- You want the most polished daily-use experience within your budget
Best Windows choice: Acer Swift Go 14
Choose this if:
- You want to stay comfortably   under budget
- You want a   portable, efficient Windows laptop
- Your workload is mainly coding, school projects, light Docker, and occasional editing
Best performance-first choice: ASUS Vivobook Pro 15
Choose this if:
- You care more about   power and storage   than portability
- You expect Docker/project loads to grow
- You can accept worse battery life
Fit Notes for Your Requirements
Context for this ranking:
- Battery claims are treated as   manufacturer-style estimates  , so real student use will usually be lower.
- “Light Docker use” means a few containers or modest local dev stacks, not heavy VM-like workloads.
